CHIEF COMPLAINT
Abnormal lab finding/elevated blood sugar

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
55-year-old male with past medical history of anxiety and epilepsy presents following emergency room visit for elevated blood sugar. Patient attributes the hyperglycemia to recent travel and hosting visitors over the past two weeks, during which he was not monitoring sugar intake and experienced increased stress. He was treated in the ER and started on metformin. Prior hemoglobin A1c values were borderline but are now elevated. Patient reports feeling well since the ER visit. Regarding anxiety, he has had some difficult moments but reports improvement, especially as the weekend approaches, and feels things are currently under control. Regarding epilepsy, patient denies recent seizure activity for several months; his last seizure was minor.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Negative for chest pain, shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, fever, or chills.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Anxiety
Epilepsy

MEDICATIONS
Metformin 500 mg twice daily
Keppra

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recent travel and hosting of visitors over the past two weeks.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs are good. Heart: regular rate and rhythm. Lungs: clear. Lower extremities: trace pitting edema noted, likely related to IV fluids received in the emergency room.

RESULTS
Blood glucose: 162 mg/dL (patient ate approximately 2 hours prior to testing)
Hemoglobin A1c: 8% (prior value approximately 6% when not on medications)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Newly diagnosed diabetes mellitus: Continue metformin 500 mg twice daily; may increase dose over time. Order hemoglobin A1c for follow-up.

2. Anxiety: Discussed potential worsening during winter months; patient willing to try new treatment approach.

3. Epilepsy: Continue Keppra. Patient is due for follow-up appointment with neurologist (last seen approximately 3 months ago).
